cases.evidence_basis_en: The adaptive menu was slower than the static comparator; the study therefore supplies route-specific negative evidence rather than missing data.
cases.evidence_basis_zh: 自适应 menu 慢于静态比较方案，因此这是路径特定的负证据，而非缺失数据。
cases.proposed_use_en: Use frequency-and-recency adaptation instead of the evaluated static split menu.
cases.proposed_use_zh: 以频率和近期使用驱动的自适应替代已评估静态 split menu。

cases.evidence_basis_en: Participants could customize effectively in the tested task, adaptable menus beat adaptive menus in some orders, and most participants preferred the adaptable condition.
cases.evidence_basis_zh: 参与者可在测试任务中有效定制；可调 menu 在部分顺序中优于自适应 menu，且多数参与者偏好可调条件。
cases.proposed_use_en: Offer user-controlled split-menu customization in the evaluated menu task.
cases.proposed_use_zh: 在已评估 menu 任务中提供用户控制的 split-menu 定制。

cases.evidence_basis_en: Compared with manufacturer defaults, the evaluated interfaces improved speed, accuracy, and satisfaction for the target population.
cases.evidence_basis_zh: 相对厂商默认界面，已评估界面改善了目标人群的速度、准确性与满意度。
cases.proposed_use_en: Generate reversible interfaces for users whose motor abilities are poorly served by manufacturer defaults.
cases.proposed_use_zh: 为不适合厂商默认界面的运动障碍用户生成可逆界面。

cases.evidence_basis_en: The adapted condition improved observed task performance and subjective experience against the non-adapted website in the evaluated sample.
cases.evidence_basis_zh: 在已评估样本中，自适应条件相对非自适应网站改善了任务表现与主观体验。
cases.proposed_use_en: Use the evaluated cultural adaptation for the tested website tasks and populations.
cases.proposed_use_zh: 在测试网站任务与人群中使用已评估文化自适应。

cases.evidence_basis_en: Two in-use cases directly examined how exposed calibration supported ownership and goal setting rather than treating calibration as hidden setup.
cases.evidence_basis_zh: 两个真实使用案例直接考察了开放校准如何支持掌控感与目标设定，而非把校准当作隐藏设置。
cases.label_zh: 用户塑造的身体传感校准
cases.proposed_use_en: Expose calibration so teachers and learners can shape goals and system behavior in the evaluated physical-skill setting.
cases.proposed_use_zh: 开放校准，使教师和学习者在已评估身体技能场景中塑造目标与系统行为。

cases.evidence_basis_en: The conservative policy was designed to avoid changes when none were beneficial and outperformed non-adaptive and frequency-based policies in the reported evaluations.
cases.evidence_basis_zh: 保守策略被设计为在无益时不改变，并在报告评估中优于非自适应与频率策略。
cases.label_zh: 保守型模型驱动 menu 自适应
cases.proposed_use_en: Use the conservative policy in the evaluated adaptive-menu setting.
cases.proposed_use_zh: 在已评估自适应 menu 场景中使用保守策略。

cases.evidence_basis_en: Participants preferred supported, transparent suggestions in interviews, but the vignettes used synthetic data and did not test a functional system or task benefit.
cases.evidence_basis_zh: 访谈参与者偏好有支持且透明的建议，但 vignette 使用合成数据，未检验功能系统或任务收益。
cases.proposed_use_en: Deploy interaction-data-driven visual personalization suggestions with user acceptance and refinement.
cases.proposed_use_zh: 部署由交互数据驱动、可由用户接受和调整的可视个性化建议。

selection.coding_boundary: Authors of the present manuscript coded public reports. The source authors did not validate these encodings, and no independent second coder was available.
selection.eligibility: Peer-reviewed HCI work with an implemented or concretely specified personalization route, an identifiable comparator or consequence, and sufficient primary-source reporting to fill the frozen route schema.
selection.strategy: Purposive maximum-variation benchmark, not a systematic review or prevalence estimate.
variation_axes: lab versus field or case-study use

sources.reported_evidence: Controlled lab study with 27 participants; static was faster than adaptive, adaptable was faster than adaptive in some orders, and most participants preferred adaptable.
sources.title: A Comparison of Static, Adaptive, and Adaptable Menus

sources.reported_evidence: Automatically generated interfaces were compared with manufacturer defaults and improved speed, accuracy, and satisfaction for people with motor impairments.
sources.title: Automatically Generating Personalized User Interfaces with Supple

sources.reported_evidence: Evaluation with 41 users found faster task performance, fewer clicks and errors, and preference for the culturally adapted website over a non-adapted version.
sources.title: Improving Performance, Perceived Usability, and Aesthetics with Culturally Adaptive User Interfaces

sources.reported_evidence: Two in-use body-sensing case studies showed teachers and pupils using exposed calibration to set goals and shape the technology to their bodies.
sources.title: Embracing Calibration in Body Sensing: Using Self-Tweaking to Enhance Ownership and Performance

sources.reported_evidence: A conservative adaptive-menu policy was evaluated empirically and in simulation against non-adaptive and frequency-based policies.
sources.title: Adapting User Interfaces with Model-based Reinforcement Learning

sources.reported_evidence: Twelve interview participants considered synthetic-data vignettes; preferences and design considerations were elicited, but no functional personalized system or real task benefit was tested.
sources.title: Exploring the Role of Interaction Data to Empower End-User Decision-Making in UI Personalization

matched_high_change.boundary_language: These are normative high-change peaks, not independently annotated semantic events.

measurement_robustness.research_question: How identifiable, parameter-robust, repeatable, and practically useful is interface-contingent temporal deviation in continuous affect reports?

simulation_recovery.design: known lag and/or slope-centered amplitude pulse across three noise levels
simulation_recovery.interpretation_boundary: Recovery diagnoses the estimator; it does not identify empirical lag as uniquely affective.

phase_gate.rule: cross-dimensional gain > 0, participant-bootstrap CI lower > 0, and circular-shift permutation p < 0.05

normative_dynamics.research_question: Do participant-specific temporal warps transfer across valence and arousal, indicating phase variation rather than mechanical DTW fit?

external_source_records.reported_evidence: Twelve interview participants considered synthetic-data vignettes; preferences and design considerations were elicited, but no functional personalized system or real task benefit was tested.
external_source_records.title: Exploring the Role of Interaction Data to Empower End-User Decision-Making in UI Personalization

external_source_records.reported_evidence: Controlled lab study with 27 participants; static was faster than adaptive, adaptable was faster than adaptive in some orders, and most participants preferred adaptable.

external_source_records.title: Embracing Calibration in Body Sensing: Using Self-Tweaking to Enhance Ownership and Performance

external_source_records.reported_evidence: Evaluation with 41 users found faster task performance, fewer clicks and errors, and preference for the culturally adapted website over a non-adapted version.
external_source_records.title: Improving Performance, Perceived Usability, and Aesthetics with Culturally Adaptive User Interfaces

external_source_records.reported_evidence: A conservative adaptive-menu policy was evaluated empirically and in simulation against non-adaptive and frequency-based policies.
external_source_records.title: Adapting User Interfaces with Model-based Reinforcement Learning

protocol_rules.design_status: Five normative design commitments synthesized from validity, HCI personalization, documentation, and algorithmic-audit literature. The sources motivate the commitments; they do not logically prove that the rules are complete or universally correct.

checked: source locators and content hashes where local artifacts exist
order invariance, malformed-record rejection, locality, and generated-file propagation
positive-permission boundary and declared precedence probes
not_checked: truth or completeness of literature coding
substantive validity of a route status or rule
human analyst agreement, completion time, or usability
fairness, user benefit, or safety outside each source's evaluated boundary

resolver.ablation_semantics: Removing a rule removes its constraint or permission. An affected route becomes unresolved unless another declared rule independently matches; ablation does not assume automatic deployment.
resolver.policy: Evaluate rules by ascending priority. The first matching constraint wins; a bounded-pass permission is returned only when no higher-priority constraint matches. No match returns a named evidence request, never silent approval.
resolver.precedence_rationale: Lifecycle obligations precede local performance; a failed route-matched comparator precedes consequence and scope; consequence mismatch precedes scope; positive permission is evaluated last. This harm-first order returns the highest-consequence unresolved obligation rather than treating priorities as empirical weights.

protocol_rules.unit_of_audit: A candidate personalization route defined by its proposed use, deployment stage, comparator, evidence boundary, consequence, and retention horizon.

category_balanced_calibration.selection: allocate videos as evenly as possible across the five released target-emotion categories; use the same fold-selected additive shrinkage as the random-calibration analysis

matched_target_trial_sensing.feature_pooling: per-trial mean and standard deviation of frozen 400-D CBraMod embeddings and 180-D released-array fNIRS summaries
matched_target_trial_sensing.outer_protocol: five participant-held-out folds; validation q and context use only outer-training participants

own_other_warp.estimand: cross-dimensional alignment gain from a receiver's own source-axis warp minus the mean gain from other held-out participants' warps in the same video and outer fold

within_video_donor_reassignment.scheme: within each outer-fold/video block, a random one-to-one derangement assigns every receiver another held-out donor

protocol.target: q_pv = trial mean of the absolute local signed temporal deviation |delta_pv(t)|

reference_composition_sensitivity.primary_reference_size: 19 outer-training participants in four folds and 20 in one fold

trajectory_geometry_adjustment.model: OLS q_pv on standardized trajectory-geometry covariates plus video fixed effects; participant variance is re-estimated from residuals

revision2_run_manifest.post_run_metadata_correction: Own-versus-other alignment advantages are in released joystick label units, not seconds; numerical arrays and inference are unchanged.

calibration_uncertainty.metric_boundary: gains are seconds-scaled aggregate q_pv prediction improvements, not millisecond local-alignment precision
calibration_uncertainty.uncertainty: bootstrap resamples participants and, within each sampled participant, one calibration-set repetition

revision3.claim_boundary: The available data support a candidate within-session, reference-relative profile. They do not establish test-retest persistence, cross-interface portability, or consequential utility.

geometry_crossfit.protocol: five participant-held-out cross-fitting folds; standardization and OLS coefficients are fitted only on training participants

feature_pooling.fnirs: per-trial mean/std plus 2,4,6,8,10-s distributed-lag cross-moments against fold-safe reference-gradient energy

unified_lopo_gstudy.estimator: balanced two-facet ANOVA method-of-moments; negative participant or video variance estimates are recorded and truncated to zero only when computing reliability

revision4.claim_boundary: The new analyses test estimator dependence and proximal trace correction. They do not add a second session, unseen interfaces, real-time inference, or observed user benefit/harm.

consensus_mapping_audit.mathematical_note: The rounded average of two nondecreasing mappings is itself nondecreasing, so cumulative-max projection is a verified no-op for all released trials. The consensus is a band-respecting summary mapping, not a claim that it is the unique original path.

dtw_objective_audit.implementation_audit: The executed and manuscript objectives directly add lambda_s for every non-diagonal transition; no division by path length occurs.

sensitivity_objectives.step_zero: sum(local+warp) with lambda_s set to zero

full_pipeline_reference_bootstrap.protocol: Participants are resampled as newly indexed pseudo-participants; each pseudo-participant's leave-one-pseudo-index reference and DTW targets are rebuilt before category-stratified video resampling.

no_sensor_baseline.decision: Video mean is the point-best no-sensor baseline; its small advantage over context is reported with paired uncertainty. Deployment should retain the best no-sensor baseline rather than assume context wins.

sampling_rate_audit.adopted_analysis_interpretation: Every EEG trial has exactly 1,000 array samples per 1-Hz label second and every stated five-second baseline has 5,000 samples. The analysis therefore treats 1,000 Hz as the released array-index density and reduces it to 200 Hz for CBraMod. This resolves internal array timing but does not assert the undocumented acquisition hardware rate.

signal_quality_audit.boundary: These are secondary array-level screens, not source acquisition QC; they do not reconstruct rereferencing, notch filtering, EOG/EMG, motion annotations, or provider-side bad-channel decisions.

eeg.thresholds: flat s.d.<0.1 microvolt; extreme peak-to-peak>500 microvolts

signed_trace_correction.endpoint: Mean absolute valence/arousal trace error against the fold-safe reference over the common 10-s interior after a constant signed timestamp correction. This is proximal trace correction, not user benefit.

revision5.claim_boundary: The added analyses use the same released session. They do not provide test-retest persistence, unseen-video validation, demographic transport, external-reference validation, hardware acquisition metadata, or user utility.

cross_video_identity_transfer.boundary: This tests cross-video transfer of a constant signed residual. It does not establish persistence of the local same-trial warp w(t), cross-session identity, or a person-intrinsic affective clock.
cross_video_identity_transfer.design: Each participant's additive residual is estimated from independent calibration videos and evaluated on that participant's held-out videos. It is compared with the video-only prediction, every other held-out participant's residual, and a within-fold deranged identity.
cross_video_identity_transfer.target: fold-safe signed bias b_pv on held-out videos

formula_target_audit.interpretation: The reviewer's missing absolute-value concern was a PDF/text-extraction misread. Source equations and saved targets use q_pv = mean_t |t-w_pv(t)| and trace MAE uses an absolute value.

full_pipeline_reference_bootstrap.cluster_exclusion_rule: For a focal pseudo-participant, every resampled copy of the same original participant is removed from the reference. Other original identities retain their cluster-bootstrap multiplicity.

generalizability_universe.finite_library_claim: The observed profile is descriptive for exactly the 15 released videos. No unseen-video population generalization is claimed.
generalizability_universe.finite_population_note: When all 15 fixed videos are treated as a census, video-sampling error is not an unseen-item uncertainty. The coefficients therefore must not be read as evidence for future videos or persistence.
generalizability_universe.random_facet_sensitivity: G/Phi are reported as method-of-moments ANOVA sensitivities to repeated participant and finite-library/category-stratified video resampling, with the five released emotion categories fixed.
generalizability_universe.variance_component_estimator: Balanced random-effects ANOVA method-of-moments. Raw negative participant/video components are recorded; truncation to zero is used only when forming reliability coefficients. This is not ML or REML.

reference_ruler_audit.boundary: The fold-common panel is independent of each held-out participant but is not an external cohort. Demographic and recruitment composition of the reference population is unavailable, preventing subgroup and transportability assessment.

reference_size_sensitivity.primary_reference_size: 19 outer-training participants in four folds and 20 in one fold

cbramod.input: Centered four-second windows, 64 released array-order channels, four one-second patches of 200 microvolt samples; boundary windows use edge repetition. No electrode remapping or channel imputation was possible because channel semantics were unavailable.
cbramod.normalization: Provider baseline mean was subtracted before caching; no additional per-window z-scoring was applied before the frozen official model.
cbramod.pooling: The frozen model returns 200-D channel-by-patch tokens. Mean and maximum over channel and patch yield 400 dimensions per label second; trial mean and standard deviation yield the reported 800 dimensions.

eeg_resampling.boxcar: five-sample block averaging from the inferred 1000-Hz arrays to 200 Hz
eeg_resampling.comparison: all targets, participant folds, fNIRS features, context features, hyperparameter grids and bootstrap settings are held fixed; only EEG resampling and EEG-derived features differ
eeg_resampling.conclusion: Strict anti-alias resampling did not reverse the sensing result: no evaluated EEG-containing method improved the context-only baseline.
eeg_resampling.fft_antialias: two-second reflection padding, zero-phase FFT low-pass, 80-Hz passband, raised-cosine 80--100-Hz transition, zero response at and above 100 Hz, then factor-five decimation

fnirs.baseline: five-second provider array mean subtracted per signal type and channel
fnirs.detrending_or_bandpass: not applied in the evaluated secondary pipeline
fnirs.motion_screen: within-array first-difference threshold = channel/type median absolute difference + 6 MAD; extreme-level screen uses |robust z|>8
fnirs.per_channel_features: 6 signal types x 5 statistics (mean, s.d., slope, skewness, excess kurtosis) x 3-second radius-one context = 90
fnirs.resampling: linear interpolation to four samples per label second
fnirs.reservation_pooling: masked channel mean and s.d. of 90 features = 180 per label second
fnirs.trial_dimension: trial mean+s.d. of 180 features (360) plus five 180-D lagged cross-moments at 2/4/6/8/10 s (900) = 1,260

signed_calibration_practical_value.burden_scope: Continuous annotation time computed from released video durations; setup, instructions, breaks, and training time are unavailable and excluded.
signed_calibration_practical_value.decision: The incremental comparison is calibrated versus video-only correction. Because no smallest worthwhile improvement was specified before seeing the data, statistical support does not establish practical value.
signed_calibration_practical_value.scale: joystick labels on the released [1,255] range

category_heterogeneity.boundary: The test concerns heterogeneity across the five categories represented by this empirical video library; it does not establish stable category traits.
category_heterogeneity.primary_effect: own residual gain versus video-only prediction
category_heterogeneity.test: 10,000 within-participant category-label permutations of the sum of squared deviations among five category mean gains

decision_threshold_curves.boundary: Thresholds are a transparent sensitivity grid because no smallest worthwhile improvement or acceptable degradation threshold was specified before analysis. The curves do not establish equivalence or practical utility.

matched_cross_video_identity_transfer.boundary: This tests cross-video transfer of a constant signed residual. It does not establish persistence of local w(t), cross-session identity, or a person-intrinsic timing trait.
matched_cross_video_identity_transfer.category_empty_cell_rule: A participant-repeat-category cell is skipped when all three videos in that category are calibration videos; skipped counts are reported.
matched_cross_video_identity_transfer.donor_matching: For each receiver repetition, every donor residual uses the receiver's exact calibration-video set, the same outer fold, and the same frozen fold/budget shrinkage value. Donors are other outer-held-out participants.
matched_cross_video_identity_transfer.inference_unit: participant; calibration repetitions are averaged within participant
matched_cross_video_identity_transfer.target: fold-safe signed bias b_pv on held-out videos

primary_antialias_reservation_sensing.boundary: The result is specific to released arrays, array-order adaptation, reservation masks, evaluated features/models, q as target, and the participant-held-out same-trial offline protocol.

decision_threshold_curve.interpretation: Conditional benefit and degradation rates across hypothetical thresholds; no threshold was prespecified and the curve is not an equivalence or practical-utility analysis.

primary_antialias_reservation_sensing.implementation_sensitivity: five-sample boxcar reduction with the same reservation-aware fNIRS

feature_pooling.cbramod: anti-aliased array-order CBraMod trial mean and s.d. (800-D)
feature_pooling.fnirs: reservation-aware trial mean/s.d. plus distributed-lag cross-moments against fold-safe reference-gradient energy (1,260-D)
feature_pooling.handcrafted_eeg: anti-aliased spectral/Hjorth trial mean and s.d. (180-D)

nested_matched_target_sensing.inner_reference_protocol: for every inner split, inner-training targets use A\{p}; inner-validation targets use A; all context, scaling and penalties are fitted without inner-validation participants
nested_matched_target_sensing.prediction_scope: participant-held-out, same-trial, offline estimation; not cold-start onboarding and not real-time inference

primary_antialias_reservation_sensing.primary_pipeline: Strict 80-Hz-passband/100-Hz-stopband anti-aliased EEG decimation combined with reservation-aware fNIRS pooling.

repeated_grouped_cv_sensitivity.boundary: This is fold-allocation sensitivity for the released 24 participants, not evidence of equivalence, external generalization, or user benefit.
repeated_grouped_cv_sensitivity.design: 5 repetitions of five-fold outer participant-grouped CV with four-fold inner participant-grouped model selection; repeat 0 is the primary allocation and later repeats use deterministic shuffles

primary_antialias_reservation_sensing.target: fold-matched primary q matrix from phase_trait_matrix.npz

revision6.reporting_boundary: Only aggregate Revision-6 results are written. Participant-level targets, predictions, calibration profiles, and participant-indexed manifests are excluded from the anonymous artifact.

siglip_feature_manifest.timestamp_convention: feature index t uses the visual frame emitted by ffmpeg fps=1 for second t; audio uses [max(0,t-window+1),t+1) with zero left-padding
